frontier.hypothesis: H8 (weak lever, worth one measurement) — struct-typed aggregate spelling. `struct { s32 a; s32 b; } dummy;` + `(void) dummy;` as a semantically-distinct aggregate might a. have the same +8 frame reservation but a different reviewer disposition (struct-shaped dead locals appear in SOTN as PSP-required carve-outs), or b. get scalarized by GCC 2.7.2 into scalars and disappear like `s32 dummy;` did.
frontier.mechanism: GCC 2.7.2 does not have full SRA but does scalarize simple aggregates whose address is not taken (via `flow_delete_insn` + register-promotion). If the struct scalarizes, the frame goes to 0 (same as scalar-dummy). If it doesn't, the frame reserves 8 bytes exactly like the array, and the review disposition question is whether SOTN treats a two-field dead struct as a distinct sanctioned family. Very unlikely to close but cheap to measure.
